messages.subject: GAM models
parts:
I have a feeling this is more of a stats question than an R question, but I am having trouble interpreting the results of some generalized additive models that I am making which use a suite of  independent variables to predict frog presence/absence in lakes that contain fish.

My basic issue is that as I add more and more variables to my model, the p-values for the individual variables tend to go down. Adding smoothing functions tends to make things worse. However, adding those variables and smoothing functions significantly increase my R-squared values and lower my AIC. I've attached some code and results as an example.

So my question is: how much do I look at p-values and how much do I just pay attention to R-squared and AIC?


--

messages.subject: Re: GAM models
parts:
Rosemary,

The function `AICctab` in the package `bblme` lets you compare models:

    library(bblme)
    AICctab(M1, M2, M3, M4, base = TRUE, weights = TRUE, nobs = nrow(dd))
    ##    AICc  df dAICc weight
    ## M4 -14.0 4    0.0 0.9261
    ## M1  -7.6 2    6.4 0.0374
    ## M3  -6.9 3    7.1 0.0262
    ## M2  -5.0 3    9.0 0.0103

Note that 
1) M1-M4 are several different models that have been fit to the data
2) This uses AICc, not AIC, which corrects for sample size
3) `nobs` is the number of observations, in this case the number of rows in dataset `dd`
4) You get comparison of AICc, the degrees of freedom, the *deviance* (difference from the min AICc) value, and the *model weights*

The model weights give you the RELATIVE strength of the models in predicting the data.  In the example above, `M4` has 93% of the weight, so one could relatively confidently select this model as "best" of that set, and examine its parameter estimates to see if they are different from zero.  If the weights are similar between models, then its best to average models together to get a best predictor.

See Chapter 5 of Rich McElreath's book, starting around page 272, for more detail on comparing models, averaging, and getting confidence intervals for parameters when averaging models.  Link to that here: http://goo.gl/QdW2l .  To use his method, you'll need to download and install the book's R package, here: http://goo.gl/QyvWj.

Thanks noam,
I think the problems I am having are in the "examine parameter estimates and see if they are different from zero" step. GAMs don't really give you parameter estimates for the smothed terms since they are non-linear. I've examined the plots, and I have the feeling the straight lines are not a good sign. But the AIC (and AICc) values say the model including three straight lines is the best fit. Anyone have any guidance there?
